preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner (or have gained ownership)

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, call the multipleBotlistAddress() function with an array containing the target victim's address and set the excluded parameter to true. This will blacklist the victim address, preventing them from making any transfers (buying/selling tokens). The exploit demonstrates unauthorized privilege escalation where the owner can arbitrarily block any address from transacting.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The TokenTool contract has a multipleBotlistAddress() function that is only callable by the owner. This function can arbitrarily blacklist any address by setting _isBlacklisted[address] = true. When an address is blacklisted, they cannot send or receive tokens due to the check in _transfer(). This demonstrates owner privilege abuse where the owner can unilaterally block any address from transacting.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Use storage slot manipulation to become the owner of the deployed contract. 2. Call multipleBotlistAddress() with the victim's address to blacklist them. 3. Verify the victim is now blacklisted.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Determine the storage slot for _owner (should be slot 0). 2. Use vm.store() to set _owner to our attacker address. 3. Create an array containing the victim address. 4. Call multipleBotlistAddress() with the array and true. 5. Check that _isBlacklisted[victim] returns true.
